header:
Meeting: Cascade Medical - security & deployment evaluation
Date/Time: 2025-09-15 15:00 UTC (scheduled 1h)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CISO, Cascade), Daniel Lee (CTO), Priya Kumar (Head of Infra), Jordan Brooks (Procurement)
summary: Discovery focused on security posture requirements for deploying Redwood-hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main concerns: SOC 2 / ISO compliance, SSO/SAML integration (Okta), RBAC and least-privilege, audit logging granularity and retention, encryption (CMEK/BYOK/HSM), data residency and retention/erasures. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 artifacts and architecture/KMS checklist; schedule technical deep dive with infra team.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 expectations
Audit logs, SIEM exports, log retention
Encryption at rest/in transit, CMEK, BYOK, HSM
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem) tradeoffs
Data retention and deletion policies (BAA / HIPAA)
transcript: 00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — Alex Chen, AE. Priya Patel from our SE team will cover the technical bits. Marta, do you want to kick off with your main concerns?

00:14 Marta (Cascade): Sure, hi — Marta Ruiz, CISO. We've been evaluating inference platforms. Primary is compliance: SOC 2, ISO, a BAA for PHI, and Okta SSO. Also we need to understand how keys are managed, like can we use our KMS or HSM?

00:34 Alex: Yep, exactly the topics we wanted to cover today. Priya will walk through the options — hosted, dedicated, or private — and how they map to controls. Quick note: transcription may flip some product names, sorry if there's any weird auto-capture errors.

00:50 Priya (Redwood): Thanks. I'll start with the high-level. Hosted is our managed API — fastest to get started, we do SOC 2 and have a Type II report. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with network isolation and predictable throughput. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. For PHI, many customers choose Private or Dedicated with a BAA.
01:24 Daniel (Cascade): Can you clarify the difference in terms of network egress? We need all traffic to stay in our VPC for certain workloads.

01:34 Priya: For Private we deploy a control plane that you manage — traffic never leaves your VPC for inference. For Dedicated, we can set up VPC peering and private endpoints; there may be managed egress for telemetry unless you opt out. We'll share the exact network diagram.
02:00 Marta: What about SOC 2 scope — does it cover the whole stack, and can we get the auditor letter?

02:12 Alex: We have SOC 2 Type II for infra and app controls; we'll send the report. We also have an ISO 27001 summary — some customers request full certification copies, we can provide summaries and auditor letters under NDA. Link we'll share: https://redwood.example/security/SOC2-2024.pdf (placeholder).

02:38 Priya: On keys — we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) and BYOK patterns. For Private, you can point to your KMS or HSM (AWS KMS, external HSM via PKCS#11). For Hosted we can support envelope encryption with customer keys, and we offer optional HSM-backed key wrapping. Key rotation, access logs, and KMS audit trails are available.
03:15 Marta: Ok, does that include FIPS validated HSMs? We need FIPS for certain contracts.

03:24 Priya: We have customers who require FIPS 140-2/3 HSMs; on Private we can integrate with your validated HSMs. On Dedicated we have options for HSM-backed key storage depending on region and purchase. We'll note specifics in the KMS checklist.
03:50 Jordan (Procurement): Timeline question — if we go Private, how long to deploy?

04:00 Priya: Typical Private deployments take 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and infra readiness. Dedicated can be 1-2 weeks for provisioning reserved capacity. Hosted is immediate. We'll include a timeline grid in the follow-up.
04:30 Daniel: Audit logging — what level of logs do you provide? We need token-level tracing, request/response metadata (not necessarily PII), and export to our SIEM.

04:42 Priya: We emit structured audit logs with request IDs, model used, latency, and token counts. We redact or avoid capturing prompt content by default unless you enable trace mode. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM (S3, CloudWatch, Splunk) and retention is configurable. We can provide event schemas.
05:20 Marta: But for PHI, we'd need full egress control and log retention for 7 years in some cases — can you meet that?

05:34 Alex: Retention windows are configurable; many customers set 30/90/365+ day retention. For long-term archive we can integrate with your storage. For BAA/HIPAA needs we support audit exports and can arrange specific retention policies. We'll share templates.

06:05 Priya: Important caveat: when you enable model debugging or full trace, the text content may be captured in logs — that's opt-in. Default analytics do token-level metrics without full prompt capture. We'll document the exact fields.
06:40 Daniel: How about RBAC? We can't have broad admin keys floating around. Need fine-grained roles, service accounts, and least privilege.

06:53 Priya: We support RBAC with roles for admin, developer, viewer, and scoped service tokens for specific routes/models. In Private you can sync groups from Okta via SAML SCIM for automated provisioning. We also support short-lived tokens and audit trails for API keys.
07:20 Marta: Do you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning? Okta is our IDP.

07:27 Alex: Yes, SSO via SAML, and user provisioning through SCIM; we'll include the Okta integration guide. Note: sometimes SCIM attributes map differently in transcription, e.g., username vs userPrincipalName. We'll send the mapping guidance.
07:48 Jordan: On procurement, do you require long-term commitments for Dedicated?
07:56 Alex: Dedicated usually comes with reserved monthly capacity pricing and a term (monthly or annual commitments). We can prototype on Hosted then move to Dedicated with a commit.

08:15 Priya: A recurring security topic: can Redwood guarantee data deletion on request? For Private, you manage deletion. For Hosted, we have documented retention/erasure procedures and support data deletion APIs and attestations. We'll include deletion SLA options.
08:45 Marta: We need a process for e-discovery and legal holds — can we freeze deletion for a given dataset?

08:56 Priya: Yes — we support legal hold flags for logs and artifacts in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we handle requests through our compliance workflow and can provide exports and retain as needed under the agreement. We'll document steps.
09:20 Daniel: Performance tradeoffs — if we encrypt everything client-side or use BYOK, is there latency impact?

09:31 Priya: There's modest overhead for client-side encryption but for typical LLM inference it's mostly key wrapping at request time, not per-token cryptography. The inference runtime uses optimized paths; for very low-latency use cases we recommend Dedicated with local keys to avoid cross-region KMS calls.
09:58 Marta: About backups and DR — responsibilities?
10:05 Priya: For Hosted, Redwood takes care of backups with RTO/RPO targets; Dedicated has configurable backups, and Private you control DR. We'll send SLA and RTO/RPO numbers.
10:35 Daniel: Any third-party pen tests or vuln scans we can review?
10:42 Alex: We do annual penetration tests and publish summaries. Full reports under NDA. We'll include contact to coordinate if you need more.
11:00 Marta: Can you integrate with our SIEM for real-time alerting? We use Splunk and Datadog.
11:08 Priya: Yes, we can stream audit logs and alerts to Splunk, Datadog, or an S3 bucket for your SIEM. We also have webhooks for alerting.
11:30 Jordan: Will legal need a BAA before we proceed?
11:37 Alex: For PHI workloads we require a BAA. We can start the BAA template in parallel with the pilot. Procurement — we'll share contract starter language.
12:00 Marta: Also curious about model governance — do you offer evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets?

12:08 Priya: That's Redwood Optimize — we do quality monitoring, regression alerts, and prompt-set based evals. Those can be run in your environment for Private or access controlled in Dedicated. We'll include docs.
12:28 Daniel: One more on keys — does Redwood ever see plaintext model inputs if CMEK is used?

12:37 Priya: For CMEK with Private, no — keys never leave your control and encryption is done in your environment. With Hosted and envelope encryption, we can ensure data is encrypted server-side and we don't retain keys if BYOK is configured. We'll document exact flows.
13:05 Marta: Can you support token-level billing and token auditing? We need to reconcile cost with usage.
13:14 Alex: Yes, the Console gives token-level breakdowns per API key and model. We can also export usage reports for chargeback. We'll demo that in the next meeting.

13:40 Priya: I want to flag a subtlety — model fallbacks. If a preferred model is unavailable we'll route to a compatible variant; that can affect data residency if routing crosses regions. You can pin regions and models to avoid that. We'll show routing policy configs.
14:08 Marta: Good — we need regional pinning for EU data.
14:15 Priya: That's supported. We'll include a routing policy example in the follow-up.
14:35 Jordan: Procurement — typical billable metrics? tokens vs reserved capacity?
14:44 Alex: Hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeddings), Dedicated is committed throughput + overage, Private is platform fee plus infra costs. We'll provide a pricing matrix.
15:05 Daniel: About audit logs — what's the retention granularity? Can we have different retention for admin vs developer logs?
15:18 Priya: Yes, retention policies can be per-log-type. Admin audit logs you might want longer retention. We'll include sample policy configs (JSON/YAML).
15:45 Marta: Do you have JIT (just-in-time) access or temporary admin elevation for support?

15:55 Alex: Support access is strictly authorized; for Hosted we have an auditable process for temporary access with justification and timebox. For Private you can decide whether Redwood support gets access; we can do session recordings and approvals.
16:20 Priya: A quick note on transcription quirks: sometimes the system turns 'KV cache' into 'KV cash' or 'HSM' into 'ham', so apologies for the transcript weirdness. We'll ensure docs are clear.
16:38 Marta: Anything else we should be aware of from a legal standpoint? Data residency, export controls?
16:47 Alex: Export controls depend on models and data; we'll provide compliance notes. For regulated data, Private is the recommended route. We'll attach our compliance pack.
17:05 Jordan: Next steps recap?

17:10 Alex: Quick recap — we'll send: SOC2 PDF, ISO summary, KMS/HSM checklist and architecture diagram, pricing matrix for Dedicated/Private, and schedule the technical deep dive. Action items in the doc.
17:30 Marta: Sounds good. Can we get the SOC2 report by Thursday?
17:36 Alex: Yes, aim to send by 2025-09-18. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive. Thanks everyone.
17:48 (call ends)
